11	
12	At a test object `T` whose underlying space is a **single point** — for the tangent-space
13	computation the two cases are the dual numbers `Spec k[ε]` and the base `Spec k` itself —
14	the coset subgroup `π_T^* Pic(T)` that the *relative* Picard functor quotients out is
15	**trivial**, so
16	
17	```
18	Pic(C ×_k T) / π_T^* Pic(T)  ≃+  Pic(C ×_k T).
19	```
20	
21	The coset calculus of `PicSharp.relPresheaf` therefore disappears from the ε-kernel
22	computation entirely, and the dual-number kernel of the *relative* functor may be computed
23	on the *absolute* Picard group, where the two-chart Čech model of
24	`Picard/Pic0DualNumberCocycle.lean` §6 lives.
25	
26	## Why this is cheap
27	
28	`IsLocallyTrivial` asks for an affine open `U ∋ x` trivialising the module. On a one-point
29	space *every* nonempty open is `⊤`, so a locally trivial module is **globally** trivial and
30	no cover-splitting argument is needed. That is the whole content: the collapse is
31	**topological**, not commutative algebra about `Pic` of an Artin local ring.
32	
33	The general-coefficient statement ("`Pic` of a finite product of Artin local rings
34	vanishes") is true, is genuine commutative algebra, and is *not needed here*.
